hypothesis: Implementing a voice cloning defense stack with tuned thresholds and step-up verification, guided by real-time telemetry and KPI monitoring, will reduce successful voice-cloning-enabled fraud and high-risk impersonation events by at least 30% without increasing average handle time by more than 5% or materially degrading customer experience metrics, relative to the existing controls baseline.

baseline.description: Current production call-handling and fraud controls without specialized AI voice cloning defenses. Environment includes standard KBA (knowledge-based authentication), basic device/ANI checks, existing fraud rules, and generic QA/recording. No dedicated synthetic voice detection, no specialized liveness prompts beyond standard scripts, and limited security-focused telemetry (e.g., fraud chargebacks, manual case flags, and aggregate call metrics).
features: No signal-level or model-based voice cloning detector in the call path.
Standard IVR and agent flows with existing KBA and one-time passwords where applicable.
Manual fraud case creation by agents or fraud ops teams in downstream case-management tools.
Existing contact center metrics (AHT, abandonment, NPS/CSAT, transfer rates) collected via CCaaS/CRM, but not linked at a per-call level to security outcomes.
Limited or no real-time risk scoring; fraud metrics are mostly lagging (e.g., confirmed losses, chargebacks).
baseline.selection_criteria: All eligible calls from predefined segments (e.g., retail banking inbound customer support for account and profile changes) that would normally be handled by the legacy control set during the experiment window and meet inclusion criteria (see workloads).
instrumentation_additions: Non-invasive telemetry hooks to log per-call identifiers, channel, line of business, high-level outcome (resolved, escalated, abandoned), and fraud investigation linkage IDs.
Tagged outcomes for fraud review (e.g., case opened, confirmed fraud, false alarm) in downstream fraud systems to support ground-truth labeling post hoc.
Privacy- and compliance-reviewed pseudonymous call IDs to allow matching between contact center logs and fraud/case outcomes.

treatment.description: Enhanced call-handling and fraud control flow that incorporates a voice cloning detection service, adaptive risk scoring, and voice-based step-up verification for high-risk scenarios, with full telemetry capture feeding metrics dashboards. The treatment arm runs concurrently with the baseline under a controlled rollout (A/B or rolling pilot) using the same population definitions and business rules aside from the added defenses.

components.name: Voice Cloning Detection Service
components.description: Real-time or near-real-time detector (built per Chapters 5–8) that scores incoming audio segments for likelihood of synthetic voice cloning.
inputs: Audio stream or buffered segments from telephony/IVR.
Call metadata (ANI/CLID, IVR path, queue, language, device type where available).
outputs: Optional feature-level traces for offline analysis.

components.name: Risk Orchestrator
components.description: Policy engine that fuses detector scores with existing fraud/risk signals and decides whether to proceed normally, trigger step-up verification, or route to a specialist.
inputs: Customer profile risk (e.g., VIP, high net worth, past fraud incidents).
Transaction intent (balance inquiry vs. high-value transfer).
Channel characteristics (call origin, time of day, geo anomalies).

components.name: Step-Up Verification / Liveness Flow
components.description: Configured per use cases from Chapter 7 to introduce additional verification challenges when risk is elevated, such as randomized phrases, callback flows, or out-of-band verification.
examples: Out-of-band approval via registered mobile app or email.
Agent scripts for high-risk impersonation cues with structured disposition logging.

components.name: Telemetry and Metrics Pipeline
components.description: Event-based telemetry that captures per-call detection scores, risk decisions, verification outcomes, and downstream business events into a metrics store and dashboard framework.
events_captured: Detector inference events (input metadata, score, version, latency).
Risk decision events (policy ID, decision type, rationale/signal contributions).
Verification events (challenge types, passes/fails, fallback paths).
Operational outcomes (handle time, transfers, escalations, abandonment).
Fraud/case outcomes (investigation opened, confirmed fraud, false positive).

treatment.selection_criteria: Calls from the same defined lines of business and risk segments as the baseline, meeting inclusion criteria, that are randomized or deterministically assigned (e.g., by customer ID modulo bucket) to the treatment arm. Customer and agent populations should be balanced across arms where possible.
guardrails: Hard caps on step-up challenge frequency per customer per time window.
Maximum allowed increase in agent workflow steps before forcing fall-back to baseline flow for that call.
Fail-open or fail-safe policies defined for detector or orchestrator outages, with telemetry on these conditions.

workloads.name: WL1_retail_banking_inbound_auth_and_profile_change
workloads.description: Inbound calls from retail banking customers performing authentication, profile changes (address, phone, email), or payment instrument updates. This workload is typically high risk for account takeover via voice cloning.
inclusion_criteria: Call type/category in CRM/IVR routing = Authentication, Profile Update, Security Question Reset, or Address/Contact Info Change.
Customer segments: All segments except those with specific legal or accessibility exemptions (e.g., regulatory constraints on voice biometrics in certain jurisdictions).
exclusion_criteria: Calls flagged as test, training, or internal QA.
Jurisdictions where synthetic voice detection or biometric-related processing is not yet legally cleared.
Known automated system-to-system calls (e.g., API-triggered notifications).

traffic_split.expected_distribution: Approximately 50/50 across baseline and treatment over the experiment window.

workloads.name: WL2_high-value_transaction_support
workloads.description: Calls involving high-dollar transactions, wire transfers, or large disbursements. Lower volume but higher fraud-loss exposure. May use a more conservative rollout pattern (e.g., pilot with 20% treatment).
inclusion_criteria: Transaction intent or queue = Wire Transfer, Large Payment, Cashier’s Check, or Similar High-Value Actions.
Transaction amount above pre-agreed threshold (e.g., local currency equivalent of USD 5,000) OR flagged as high risk by existing fraud engine.
exclusion_criteria: Jurisdictions or product lines outside agreed regulatory scope.
VIP/concierge service segments where additional CX approvals are needed (may be handled via separate experiment).

traffic_split.method: Stratified random sampling by risk tier
traffic_split.treatment_bucket: 20% of eligible calls, with option to gradually increase share as safety is demonstrated.
traffic_split.notes: Maintain similar distribution of risk tiers across arms using existing fraud scores for stratification.

randomization: Deterministic, data-driven assignment (e.g., hash of customer ID or anonymized token) to ensure that each returning customer consistently experiences the same arm during the experiment, avoiding contamination from mixed experiences.
Randomization logic implemented in IVR or routing layer prior to invocation of detection logic, logged for audit.
covariate_balance: Pre-experiment analysis to confirm that baseline and treatment arms have comparable distributions of customer segments (age bands, tenure, product mix), historical fraud risk scores, and typical call reasons.
If imbalance is detected, adjust via stratified sampling or weighted analysis in the experiment evaluation.
seasonality_and_time_controls: Run experiment for a minimum of 4–6 weeks to span typical intra-week patterns and avoid overly short-term anomalies.
Ensure both arms are live throughout the same time window; do not run baseline and treatment sequentially.
Track and annotate major events that may impact call volume or fraud patterns (e.g., marketing campaigns, holidays).
policy_consistency: Aside from voice defense capabilities and associated flows, all other agent scripts, offers, and core business policies remain identical across arms.
Training/briefing for agents conducted such that they understand both arms but do not selectively deviate from assigned flows.
privacy_and_compliance: Legal review of telemetry fields and retention settings before experiment start.
Explicit approvals for any processing that may be interpreted as biometric under local law, with consent handling aligned as per Chapter 9.
Anonymization or pseudonymization of call identifiers in the analytics data store, with separate mapping held under stricter access controls.
operational_safety: Real-time monitoring of key leading safety indicators (e.g., sudden spike in denial of legitimate high-risk transactions, unusual abandonment in treatment) with pre-defined rollback thresholds.
Ability to disable detector enforcement (reverting to baseline) via configuration toggle while continuing to log telemetry where permissible for diagnostic purposes.

metrics.name: successful_voice_cloning_enabled_fraud_rate
metrics.definition: Number of confirmed fraud cases in which investigators attribute a significant role to suspected or confirmed AI voice cloning divided by total eligible calls for that workload and arm, over the experiment window.
metrics.source: Fraud/case management system joined with call logs and investigator annotations (manual classification of whether synthetic voice was involved).
metrics.notes: Given attribution difficulty, use structured investigator fields (e.g., 'voice cloning suspected: yes/no/unknown') and sensitivity analysis that treats 'unknown' separately.

metrics.name: gross_fraud_loss_rate
metrics.definition: Total confirmed fraud financial losses associated with the eligible workload and arm divided by total monetary value of authorized high-risk transactions during the experiment window.
metrics.source: Core banking/payments systems combined with fraud resolution outcomes and call linkage.

metrics.name: detected_suspicious_call_rate
metrics.definition: Number of calls where the synthetic_voice_score exceeds the configured high-risk threshold or where the risk orchestrator flags the call as 'elevated risk' due at least in part to voice analysis, divided by total eligible calls.

metrics.name: step_up_verification_trigger_rate
metrics.definition: Number of calls in which any step-up verification flow is triggered (voice or non-voice) divided by total eligible calls in that arm.
metrics.source: Verification event logs and IVR/agent workflows.

metrics.name: step_up_verification_failure_rate
metrics.definition: Number of calls in which step-up verification is triggered and the customer fails or abandons the verification (excluding technical failures), divided by total step-up attempts.
metrics.source: Verification flow telemetry and call outcomes.

metrics.name: false_positive_flag_rate
metrics.definition: Among calls later adjudicated as legitimate (no fraud) and where investigators or QA agents review the interaction, proportion of calls that were flagged as suspicious by detection/orchestration.
metrics.source: Join between detector flags and human-reviewed labels for a statistically representative subsample of calls.

metrics.name: false_negative_estimate_rate
metrics.definition: Among confirmed fraudulent calls in the workload and arm, proportion with no high-risk flag from the detector/orchestrator at the time of call.
metrics.source: Join between confirmed fraud cases and detection logs; may be a lower bound given imperfect labeling.

metrics.name: average_handle_time
metrics.definition: Average duration of eligible calls from agent answer to end-of-call for that arm and workload.

metrics.name: customer_experience_score
metrics.definition: Post-call customer satisfaction or NPS-like score collected via IVR, SMS, or email survey, aggregated for eligible calls by arm.
metrics.source: Survey platform joined to call IDs.

metrics.name: call_abandonment_rate
metrics.definition: Proportion of eligible calls in which the caller hangs up before resolving their request, especially during or shortly after step-up verification prompts.
metrics.source: IVR and CCaaS call state logs, annotated by phase of call when abandonment occurred.

metrics.name: agent_escalation_rate
metrics.definition: Rate at which agents escalate calls to supervisors or fraud specialists due to suspected impersonation or confusion related to step-up verification.
metrics.source: Agent desktop disposition codes, supervisor queue entries.

metrics.name: detector_inference_latency
metrics.definition: End-to-end latency from audio frame availability to receipt of detection score at the orchestrator.
metrics.source: Telemetry emitted by detection service and orchestrator (traces).

metrics.name: human_review_workload
metrics.definition: Total human time spent per unit period on reviewing flagged calls (QA, fraud analysts, supervisors), normalized by number of eligible calls.
metrics.source: Case management tools, QA platforms, and time-tracking tags for review tasks.

primary: A relative reduction of at least 30% in successful_voice_cloning_enabled_fraud_rate in the treatment arm compared to the baseline arm for WL1 (retail inbound auth/profile change) over the experiment window, with statistical significance at p <= 0.05 or credible interval excluding zero under agreed statistical framework.
No more than a 5% relative increase in average_handle_time in the treatment arm vs baseline for WL1, with confidence intervals bounded within this threshold.

No statistically significant degradation (or at most a 5% relative decrease) in customer_experience_score for WL1 between treatment and baseline, after controlling for confounders such as call reason and customer segment.
secondary: A statistically significant decrease in gross_fraud_loss_rate in treatment vs baseline for WL2 (high-value transactions), even if the absolute number of cases is low, supported by effect-size estimates and scenario-based extrapolation.
Step_up_verification_failure_rate remains below an agreed threshold (e.g., 10–15% depending on use case) and is not materially higher in low-risk segments than in high-risk segments.

False_positive_flag_rate in treatment remains within an acceptable band defined by fraud and operations leadership (e.g., <= 2–3% of reviewed legitimate calls), or reductions in fraud losses justify higher false positive levels as per pre-defined cost-benefit thresholds.
Human_review_workload increase is bounded by available operational capacity (e.g., not more than +20% review minutes per 1k calls) or justified by proportional fraud loss reductions.
decision_rules: If primary fraud reduction and CX/operational bounds are met: recommend progressive scale-up of treatment to a larger share of traffic and/or additional workloads.
If fraud reduction is material but CX/operational impact exceeds thresholds: iterate on threshold tuning, flow design, and targeted risk segments; run follow-up experiment with adjusted parameters.
If fraud reduction is non-material or negative: halt scale-up, revert to baseline flows, and use telemetry to diagnose failure modes (e.g., detector underperformance, adversarial adaptation).

failure_modes.name: adversarial_adaptation
failure_modes.description: Attackers change tactics in response to deployment, for example by using more advanced voice cloning tools, mixing natural and synthetic voice segments, or shifting to non-voice channels.
indicators: Rising false_negative_estimate_rate over time within the treatment arm.
Significant change in distribution of synthetic_voice_score among confirmed fraud calls.
Shifts in channel or intent distribution for fraud cases (e.g., more fraud in web or chat).
mitigations: Introduce continuous adversarial evaluation per Chapter 14 and adapt detector ensembles.
Revisit thresholds and incorporate additional behavioral or metadata signals.
Update fraud strategy to treat cross-channel displacement as part of the impact model.

failure_modes.name: agent_behavior_drift
failure_modes.description: Agents may over-rely on, underuse, or misinterpret detection and risk signals, leading to inconsistent application of policies and contamination of results.
indicators: High variance in step_up_verification_trigger_rate across agents controlling for risk score.
Qualitative feedback indicating confusion about what detector or risk scores mean.
Unusually high manual overrides of orchestrator decisions.
mitigations: Standardize agent guidance and scripts; add just-in-time help text in agent desktop.
Instrument and track manual override events; add governance review for outliers.
Shadow QA review of a random sample of treatment-arm calls to ensure protocol adherence.

failure_modes.name: telemetry_gaps_or_data_quality_issues
failure_modes.description: Incomplete or inconsistent telemetry prevents accurate measurement of fraud, CX, or operational metrics.
indicators: Significant fraction of calls missing event linkage across systems (no common call ID).
Unexplained discrepancies between contact center metrics and fraud system counts.
Detector logs missing for periods of time or subsets of traffic.
mitigations: Implement data completeness checks and alerts in the telemetry pipeline.
Run periodic reconciliation reports across systems; halt interpretation of metrics when gaps exceed defined thresholds.
Use canary traffic (known test calls) to validate end-to-end logging paths regularly.

failure_modes.name: privacy_or_regulatory_noncompliance
failure_modes.description: Aggregation and use of telemetry or detection signals may inadvertently violate data protection, biometric, or consent requirements.
indicators: Legal or privacy review flags on telemetry fields or retention practices.
Customer complaints or regulatory inquiries referencing synthetic voice or biometric processing.
Discovery that calls from restricted jurisdictions or segments were included unintentionally.
mitigations: Pre-experiment privacy impact assessments and regulatory review with explicit scope definitions.
Geofencing and segment-based routing to ensure only allowed calls are included.
Strict access controls, minimization, and retention policies for telemetry data.

failure_modes.name: capacity_and_workload_overload
failure_modes.description: Increased step-up verification and human review of suspicious calls overload agents, supervisors, or fraud teams.
indicators: Human_review_workload significantly exceeds pre-defined capacity thresholds.
Rising agent_escalation_rate without clear fraud justification.
Agent-reported burnout or performance degradation in treatment queues.
mitigations: Introduce caps on daily step-up triggers and flagged calls per queue.
Prioritize high-value or high-risk segments for full treatment; leave low-risk segments at baseline.
Iterate on detector thresholds to reduce low-yield alerts.

failure_modes.name: technical_instability_or_latency_impact
failure_modes.description: Detector or telemetry services fail, degrade, or introduce latency that harms customer experience.
indicators: Spikes in detector_inference_latency, especially at p95/p99.
Increased call drop or abandonment rates during or immediately after detection phases.
Higher than expected rates of fail-open/override events due to service unavailability.
mitigations: Autoscaling, circuit breakers, and fallback strategies defined and tested before rollout.
Latency monitoring with paging thresholds and clear incident response runbooks.
Staged rollout with performance testing at expected and peak traffic levels.

infrastructure: Production-like contact center and telephony environment (CCaaS platform, IVR, agent desktops) capable of routing traffic based on experiment arm assignment.
Voice cloning detection service deployed as a scalable microservice or managed function, with secure network connectivity to telephony/IVR stack.
Risk orchestration layer (may be an existing policy engine or new microservice) capable of consuming detection scores and emitting decisions in near-real-time.

Telemetry pipeline (e.g., event bus such as Kafka or Kinesis; or CCaaS-native streaming) forwarding structured events to a data warehouse (e.g., BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift) or time-series store (e.g., Prometheus, Elasticsearch).
Dashboarding and analytics tools (e.g., Looker, Power BI, Tableau, or Grafana) connected to the telemetry store.
data_requirements: Access to pseudonymized call logs and associated metadata (timestamps, call IDs, queues, agent IDs).
Access to downstream fraud and case management systems for labeling confirmed fraud and suspected voice cloning involvement.
Customer experience survey data linked via call IDs, with opt-in rates tracked.
Compliance-approved schema for storing detection scores and verification events.
security_and_access: Role-based access control for experiment artifacts and dashboards, segregating production PII from analytics environments.
Audit logging for configuration changes to detectors, orchestrator rules, and routing logic.
Secure secrets management for any model or vendor keys (e.g., if third-party detection APIs are used).
organizational: Cross-functional experiment working group including representatives from fraud/risk, contact center operations, security architecture, data science/ML, compliance/privacy, and legal.
Defined on-call or escalation paths for experiment-related operational incidents.
Training material and briefings for agents on new flows and how to interpret risk signals where exposed.
reference_repository_integration: Cloned or forked version of the companion repository (https://github.com/bookauthority/securing-call) with the Chapter 12 / experiments folder checked out.
Configuration files in the repo mapped to the organization’s specific CCaaS, messaging, and data warehouse endpoints.
CI/CD or deployment scripts to roll out configuration updates and detector version changes in a controlled manner.

run_instructions: Design_and_Approval
1. Define target workloads (e.g., WL1, WL2) and document inclusion/exclusion criteria with fraud and operations stakeholders.
2. Conduct a privacy and legal review of the planned telemetry fields, thresholds, and step-up verification flows; update consent/disclosure scripts as needed.
3. Draft and agree on experiment parameters: traffic split percentages, duration (minimum 4–6 weeks), participating regions, and success/failure thresholds.
4. Establish experiment governance: assign an experiment owner, data analyst, operational liaison, and legal/privacy point of contact.
Instrumentation_and_Telemetry_Setup
5. Implement or configure a pseudonymous call ID that persists through IVR, CCaaS, agent desktop, and case/fraud systems; update logging configurations accordingly.

6. Deploy or enable the telemetry pipeline from the CCaaS/IVR to the data warehouse/time-series store, following the schemas defined in the evidence_schema (e.g., detection_event, risk_decision_event).
7. Integrate fraud/case management system exports with call IDs or mapping tables; schedule regular ETL jobs into the analytics environment.
8. Configure survey tools to tag post-call CX responses with the same call IDs or a joinable key; test end-to-end joins in a staging environment.
Baseline_and_Treatment_Flow_Implementation
9. Implement the voice cloning detection service as defined in Chapters 5–8 (or integrate an external API), instrumenting it with per-call inference events and latency metrics.
10. Implement the risk orchestration rules for the treatment arm, including thresholds for synthetic_voice_score, integration with existing risk scores, and definition of step-up flow triggers.

11. Define at least one voice or non-voice step-up verification flow (e.g., dynamic passphrase, out-of-band approval) and implement it in the IVR and/or agent scripts, with structured outcome logging.

12. For the baseline arm, ensure that no new detection-triggered step-up flows are used; only the existing standard flows should apply, though telemetry instrumentation should still log relevant outcomes.
Randomization_and_Routing
13. Implement deterministic assignment logic in the IVR or routing layer (e.g., hash(customer_id) % 2) to assign each eligible call to baseline or treatment.
14. Log the assigned arm (baseline/treatment) in all downstream systems via the shared call ID.

15. Validate assignment balance by running a short dry-run period (e.g., 1–2 days) where no treatment-specific logic is activated but routing and logging are fully operational; inspect arm distributions.
Pilot_and_Safety_Checks

16. Start with a limited pilot (e.g., 10–20% of eligible traffic into treatment) for WL1 and WL2, with real-time monitoring of detector_inference_latency, call_abandonment_rate, and any unexpected call routing issues.
17. If safety indicators remain within pre-agreed bounds after a short pilot window (e.g., 3–5 business days), ramp the treatment arm to the full intended share (e.g., 50% for WL1, 20% for WL2).
Experiment_Run
18. Run the experiment for the agreed period, ensuring both arms are always active during the same calendar windows.
19. Monitor leading indicators daily or weekly (technical stability, CX, and operational load), and only inspect fraud outcomes at pre-defined intervals to avoid premature stopping biases.

20. Maintain a change log; avoid making mid-experiment changes to thresholds, flows, or randomization logic unless necessary for safety. Any changes must be time-stamped and annotated for later analysis.
Analysis

21. After the experiment window, freeze configuration and extract event tables (e.g., calls, detection_events, risk_decision_events, verification_events, fraud_outcomes, cx_surveys) from the data warehouse.
22. Use the analysis notebooks or scripts in the repository’s Chapter 12 folder to:
a. Join events into per-call records and compute defined metrics for each arm and workload.
b. Assess randomization balance across arms on key covariates.
c. Estimate relative and absolute differences in primary and secondary metrics between arms, with confidence intervals or Bayesian credible intervals.
23. Perform subgroup analyses by customer segment, risk level, and geography to identify heterogeneous treatment effects and potential fairness or bias concerns.
Interpretation_and_Decision
24. Compare experimental results against the predefined success_criteria and decision_rules, explicitly noting any tradeoffs between fraud reduction, CX, and operational load.
25. Document interpreted findings, including limitations (e.g., limited fraud event counts, attribution ambiguity, suspected adversarial adaptation).
26. Present results and recommendations to the cross-functional steering group (fraud, CX, security, compliance, legal) and agree on next steps: scale-up, iterate and re-run, or rollback.
Hardening_and_Rollout

27. If the treatment is adopted, transition from experiment mode to standard operations, including updated playbooks, SLAs for detector performance, and integration of metrics into ongoing monitoring dashboards.
28. Archive experiment configurations, code versions, and metrics snapshots for auditability and future benchmarking against subsequent experiments.
29. Update the enterprise measurement framework and dashboards to incorporate the most informative metrics discovered during the experiment and to support continuous monitoring of adaptive threats.

tables.name: calls
tables.description: One record per eligible call included in the experiment, with assignment, workload, and basic call context.

fields.name: call_id
fields.description: Pseudonymous unique identifier for the call, consistent across systems.

fields.name: customer_id_hash
fields.description: Hashed or tokenized customer identifier used for randomization; not directly identifying.

fields.name: experiment_arm
fields.description: Randomization assignment for the call.

fields.name: workload_id
fields.description: Workload classification for the call.

fields.name: timestamp_start
fields.description: Call start time.

fields.name: timestamp_end
fields.description: Call end time.

fields.name: queue_or_skill
fields.description: Queue or skill-based routing identifier.

fields.name: agent_id_hash
fields.description: Hashed agent identifier for aggregate analysis.

fields.name: call_outcome
fields.description: High-level call outcome from CCaaS/CRM.

fields.name: average_handle_time_sec
fields.description: Handle time in seconds for the call.

tables.name: detection_events
tables.description: One record per detection inference for a call; some calls may have multiple events if streaming segments are scored.

fields.name: detection_event_id
fields.description: Unique identifier for the detection event.

fields.name: call_id
fields.description: Foreign key to calls.call_id.

fields.name: model_version
fields.description: Version or hash of the detection model used.

fields.name: synthetic_voice_score
fields.description: Score in [0,1] representing likelihood of synthetic voice.

fields.name: risk_band
fields.description: Binned risk assessment from the detector or orchestration.

fields.name: latency_ms
fields.description: Detection inference latency in milliseconds.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.description: Time when detection event occurred.

tables.name: risk_decision_events
tables.description: Decisions from the risk orchestration layer for each call.

fields.name: risk_decision_event_id
fields.description: Unique identifier for the decision event.

fields.name: call_id
fields.description: Foreign key to calls.call_id.

fields.name: decision
fields.description: Risk-based decision applied to the call.

fields.name: decision_reason_codes
fields.description: List of codes indicating which signals contributed (e.g., DETECTOR_HIGH_SCORE, HIGH_VALUE_TRANSACTION).

fields.name: timestamp
fields.description: Time the decision was made.

tables.name: verification_events
tables.description: Records of step-up verification attempts and outcomes during calls.

fields.name: verification_event_id
fields.description: Unique identifier for the verification event.

fields.name: call_id
fields.description: Foreign key to calls.call_id.

fields.name: verification_type
fields.description: Type of step-up verification performed.

fields.name: outcome
fields.description: Outcome of the verification attempt.

fields.name: timestamp_start
fields.description: Verification start time.

fields.name: timestamp_end
fields.description: Verification end time.

tables.name: fraud_outcomes
tables.description: Confirmed fraud and investigation outcomes linked back to calls.

fields.name: fraud_case_id
fields.description: Identifier for the fraud or investigation case.

fields.name: call_id
fields.description: Foreign key to calls.call_id; may be null if fraud not linked to a call.

fields.name: fraud_confirmed
fields.description: Whether fraud was confirmed after investigation.

fields.name: fraud_loss_amount
fields.description: Monetary loss associated with the case, in base currency.

fields.name: suspected_voice_cloning_involved
fields.description: Investigator assessment of whether voice cloning was involved.

fields.name: case_close_timestamp
fields.description: Time when the investigation was completed.

fields.name: survey_response_id
fields.description: Unique identifier for the survey response.

fields.name: call_id
fields.description: Foreign key to calls.call_id.

fields.name: survey_type
fields.description: Type of survey instrument.

fields.name: score
fields.description: Numerical score (e.g., 1–5 or -100–100), to be normalized in analysis.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.description: Time when the survey response was recorded.

tables.name: human_review_sessions
tables.description: Records of human review of calls (QA, fraud analysts, supervisors) for workload tracking.

fields.name: review_session_id
fields.description: Identifier for the review session.

fields.name: call_id
fields.description: Foreign key to calls.call_id.

fields.name: reviewer_role
fields.description: Role of the person performing the review.

fields.name: review_duration_minutes
fields.description: Approximate active time spent reviewing the call.

fields.name: label_legitimacy
fields.description: Reviewer assessment of call legitimacy.

fields.name: label_voice_cloning_suspected
fields.description: Reviewer assessment of whether voice cloning appears to be present.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.description: Timestamp of the review.

versioning.change_control: All changes to schema must be documented with date, rationale, and impact on comparability to previous experiments.

pseudonymization_requirements: All direct identifiers (names, raw phone numbers, account numbers, email addresses) must be removed or hashed before data enters experiment analytics tables.
Mapping tables from hashed IDs to real identifiers must be stored in a separate, access-restricted system and not used for routine experiment analysis.
privacy.data_retention: Define a maximum retention period (e.g., 12–24 months) for experiment tables, after which data must be purged or irreversibly anonymized, subject to legal hold requirements.
